project.title: Let the Raptures Commence
project.description: 8 × 45min British black comedy. Four billion people sorted by a child's layout decision. Eight episode outlines; Episode One revised to 42min with washing up (26 shots, FIX 4 — the pendant is her mother's, she always had it), Danny and Jodie (21) and the cops' second beat (6); ep3 cold open angels 15 shots; ep4 Pat cold open dusk 16 shots continuous into Scene 2 the old lady 35 shots, then Nina's thread retained and fully boarded — the housing estate (36), the doorstep (32) and the kitchen (24); ep5 therapy class 26 shots and the night at Pat's 51 shots, no CCTV, two grammars only. Fixes: prologue 12 pockets the tracker plus the 24f flash, shot 31 cut ERROR to UNDO?, Ep1 Sc3 shot 18 cut with 23-24 in her own room, Martin's auction marked pre-rapture, Ep3 meeting trimmed to recruitment only.

episode.title: Episode 1 — No mechanism revealed
episode.description:
45-minute episode outline, not a completed shooting script.

The mugging. Nina Sc 1 — St Jude's and the rapture. The cops — birds, arrest ourselves, the taser. Nina Sc 3 — washing up and aftermath, the pendant (her mother's, always had it, not Deborah's bedside), the first vision, she drives. Martin's auction — marked as pre-rapture flashback, since the machine must have been in Max's room for eight weeks. Then Danny and Jodie — first appearance, three weeks in, they do this now and she's better at it (handheld, tight, dark, red practical light, never a clean wide). Then the cops second beat — static two-shot from the bonnet, same bottle untouched, ends comic thread worse than it started (ninety seconds). Tag: 1980, ending on NO. Roughly 42 minutes before tag.

LET THE RAPTURES COMMENCE
EPISODE ONE — DANNY AND JODIE

INT./EXT. A HOUSE — DUSK
Cast: DANNY (40), JODIE (11)
Grammar: handheld, tight, dark, red practical light. Never a clean wide.

This is three weeks in and it's their first appearance. It should establish only two things: they do this now, and she's better at it.


1. EXT. BACK GARDEN — HANDHELD, 35mm, dusk
A fence. Danny goes over it badly, catching his coat. Jodie goes over it in one movement and waits.

2. HANDHELD — 28mm, close, the back door
He's got a screwdriver in the frame. It isn't going well. She watches.
   JODIE: It's not that sort of lock.
   DANNY: It is.
   JODIE: It's the other sort.

3. INSERT — 85mm, handheld
The screwdriver slips. His knuckle goes into the frame.

4. HANDHELD — 28mm
Jodie leans past him, does something to the handle, and the door opens.

5. HANDHELD CLOSE — 50mm
Danny holding a screwdriver, looking at an open door.
   DANNY: It was already —
   JODIE: Mm.

6. INT. KITCHEN — HANDHELD, 28mm, red torchlight
Inside. Close and shifting. A cupboard door, a corner of worktop, half a calendar. Never the room.
   DANNY: (low) Rules.
   JODIE: (recited, bored) Nothing off anyone still alive. Nothing off the dead that's got a name on it. No upstairs.
   DANNY: And?
   JODIE: And check the cistern.

7. INSERT — 100mm macro, handheld
Cupboards opening. Tins. A great deal of chutney. Nothing useful.

8. HANDHELD — 35mm
Danny finds a four-pint bottle of water at the back of a cupboard. Half full. He's thrilled and trying not to show it.

9. HANDHELD CLOSE — 50mm, on JODIE
She's looking at the ceiling.
   JODIE: There's a coat on the bannister.
   DANNY: So?
   JODIE: It's a going-out coat.

10. HANDHELD — 28mm
He stops. Listens. The house is completely still.
   DANNY: They're gone.
   JODIE: You don't know that.
   DANNY: Everyone's gone.
   JODIE: Not everyone.

11. HANDHELD — 35mm, hallway, very dark
Jodie goes toward the downstairs loo. Her bike light swings across a wall of framed photographs. Twenty of them, the same two people.

12. HANDHELD CLOSE — 50mm
She stops. Not moved. Assessing.
   JODIE: (calling, not loud) Dad.
   DANNY: (o.s.) What.
   JODIE: How many people d'you reckon are still here?
   DANNY: (o.s.) Don't know.
   JODIE: One in ten? One in twenty?
   DANNY: (o.s.) Do the cistern, Jodie.

13. INSERT — 85mm, handheld
The cistern lid off. She dips a bottle and fills it, entirely unbothered.

14. HANDHELD — 28mm, kitchen
A sound upstairs. One dull thump.

15. HANDHELD CLOSE — 50mm, on DANNY
Rigid. Not brave.

16. HANDHELD — 28mm, foot of the stairs
The two of them, close, whispering.
   DANNY: Out. Now.
   JODIE: It'll be a cat.
   DANNY: Out.
   JODIE: It's always a cat.
   DANNY: (hissing) One time it wasn't a cat.

17. HANDHELD — 35mm, up the stairwell, red, nothing visible
Hold. Then another thump, and something falling over.

18. HANDHELD — chaotic, 28mm
They go, fast and badly, knocking into things. He drops the screwdriver. She doesn't drop the water.

19. EXT. ALLEY — HANDHELD, 35mm
Both against a wall, breathing hard. Bags between their feet.
   JODIE: It was a cat.
   DANNY: You don't know that.
   JODIE: (holding up the cistern bottle) We could've had the upstairs one. Header tank's better.
   DANNY: (a beat) What's a header tank?
   JODIE: (genuinely pleased) Exactly.

20. HANDHELD CLOSE — 50mm, on DANNY
A man who has just been overtaken by his eleven-year-old and is deciding whether to acknowledge it.
   DANNY: Don't tell anyone about the door.

21. HANDHELD WIDE — 28mm, alley
The two of them walking away, red bike light bobbing, bags in hand. A completely dark street.
Hold.


LET THE RAPTURES COMMENCE
EPISODE ONE — THE COPS, SECOND BEAT

INT. POLICE CAR — NIGHT (PARKED)
Cast: KATH (30s), RAY (30s)
Grammar: static two-shot from the bonnet. The same bottle of water in the cup holder, untouched.

Short — ninety seconds. Its only job is to end the episode's comic thread on a worse note than it started.


1. STATIC TWO-SHOT — 32mm, locked off, through the windscreen
Dark. Both of them lit by the dashboard. Kath eating. Ray not.

Hold. Four seconds.
   KATH: He'll be all right, that lad.
   RAY: Which lad?
   KATH: The one from the car park.
   RAY: He was thirty-odd.
   KATH: He looked younger.
   RAY: They do.

(Pause. Six seconds.)
   KATH: I only tasered him.
   RAY: I know.
   KATH: People get tasered.
   RAY: They do.

2. STATIC WIDE — 24mm, exterior, from across the road
The car, alone, parked across two bays in an empty street. Interior light on.

3. STATIC TWO-SHOT — as 1
   RAY: There's a form.
   KATH: Ray.
   RAY: I'm only saying there's a form.
   KATH: (a beat) Have you got the form?
   RAY: (immediately) No.

(Pause.)
   KATH: Then there isn't a form.

4. INSERT — 85mm, static
The bottle in the cup holder. Neither of them has drunk any of it.

5. STATIC TWO-SHOT — as 1
Hold. Five seconds.
   RAY: Kath.
   KATH: Mm.
   RAY: Who do you think's in charge now?
   KATH: (no hesitation whatsoever) Us.

6. STATIC WIDE — 24mm, exterior — same framing as shot 2
The car in an empty street, interior light on, two people sat in it.
Hold. CUT.

# LET THE RAPTURES COMMENCE
## EPISODE 1 — SCENE 3 — WASHING UP (revised — FIX 4)

Scene: INT./EXT. ST JUDE'S — DAY
Cast: NINA (45)
Grammar: locked off, wide, deep focus, daylight, symmetrical. The camera never follows Nina. Long lenses for the road. Only the vision is handheld. Dry and procedural; Nina is unimpressed throughout, never amazed or afraid.

Fix: pendant is her mother's and she's always had it, so she doesn't find it on anyone's bedside. Shot 18 (the pendant among a dead woman's things) is cut. Shots 23–24 replaced — 23 STATIC MEDIUM 50mm her own room, 24 CLOSE 65mm picks up practical decision. Vision beat unchanged: corridor, hand to chest, first time.

---

1. STATIC WIDE — 35mm, locked off — INT. ST JUDE'S HALL — DAY
The hall after the rapture. Chairs stacked against the wall. A mop bucket in the middle of the floor. On a clipboard by the door, one ignored complaint about water pressure from earlier — still there. Hold.

2. STATIC MEDIUM — 50mm, locked off — INT. KITCHEN — DAY
Nina washing up. Methodical. The tap runs brown, then clear. She doesn't react. Stacks a plate. The radio is off.

3. STATIC MEDIUM — 50mm, locked off — INT. KITCHEN — DAY
She dries the plates with a tea towel that says ST JUDE'S. Folds it afterwards, square. Puts it back on its hook.

4. STATIC WIDE — 35mm, locked off — INT. HALL — DAY
She collects mugs from the hall. Three of them, all with different slogans. She carries them two at a time, like someone who has done this every day for years.

5. STATIC MEDIUM — 50mm, locked off — INT. UTILITY — DAY
She checks the water butt by the back door. Half full. She tops up two bottles from it, labels them with masking tape: KITCHEN.

6. INSERT — 85mm, static — INT. UTILITY
The masking tape roll. The marker pen. Her handwriting, practical, small.

7. STATIC WIDE — 35mm, locked off — INT. CORRIDOR — DAY
She pushes a mop down the corridor. The corridor is long, symmetrical, daylight from high windows. She doesn't look into the rooms as she passes.

8. STATIC MEDIUM — 50mm, locked off — INT. CORRIDOR — DAY
She stops outside Deborah's old room. Door ajar. She looks in for a second, then keeps going. No pendant here. No bedside rummage.

9. STATIC MEDIUM — 50mm, locked off — INT. STORE CUPBOARD — DAY
She counts tins. Writes a number on the clipboard. Tins, not water. Water is separate.

10. STATIC WIDE — 35mm, locked off — INT. CHAPEL — DAY
The chapel, empty. Six chairs. A wooden cross on the wall, slightly crooked. She straightens it without thinking.

11. STATIC MEDIUM — 50mm, locked off — INT. OFFICE — DAY
She opens a filing cabinet. Inside, a list of residents with dates. She crosses out two names with a biro. No ceremony.

12. STATIC MEDIUM — 50mm, locked off — EXT. ST JUDE'S — DAY
Daylight, overcast. She carries a black bag to the bins. The street outside is empty. No cars. She doesn't look up.

13. STATIC WIDE — 35mm, locked off — INT. LAUNDRY — DAY
She folds laundry. Someone else's. She folds it anyway. Puts it on a pile.

14. STATIC MEDIUM — 50mm, locked off — INT. LAUNDRY — DAY
The pile. She looks at it for a second, then leaves it. Someone will want it later, or they won't.

15. STATIC MEDIUM — 50mm, locked off — INT. CORRIDOR — DAY
She checks the fire exit. Locked. She checks the log book. Signs it.

16. STATIC WIDE — 35mm, locked off — INT. CORRIDOR — DAY
She stands in the corridor, alone. Listens. Nothing. She goes to her own room.

17. STATIC MEDIUM — 50mm, locked off — INT. NINA'S ROOM — DAY
Her own room at St Jude's. Narrow single bed, made. Wooden cross on the wall, slightly crooked. A bedside drawer. She opens it.

18. CUT — Shot 18 is cut. Previously: pendant among a dead woman's things (Deborah's bedside). Removed — pendant is her mother's, always had it. No pendant found on anyone's bedside. This slot holds the cut.

19. STATIC MEDIUM — 50mm, locked off — INT. NINA'S ROOM — DAY
She rummages in the drawer for torch batteries. Elastic bands, receipts, a rosary with a broken link, a nail file. She moves them aside.

20. INSERT — 85mm, static — INT. NINA'S ROOM
The torch, open. Batteries dead. She tips them into the bin.

21. STATIC MEDIUM — 50mm, locked off — INT. NINA'S ROOM
She looks for new batteries. The drawer is a mess. She sighs, not annoyed, just occupied.

22. STATIC MEDIUM — 50mm, locked off — INT. NINA'S ROOM
She finds a pack of batteries at the back of the drawer. Holds them up to the light. Checks the date on them.

23. STATIC MEDIUM — 50mm, locked off, her own room at St Jude's
A narrow single bed, made. A wooden cross on the wall, slightly crooked. She opens a bedside drawer. Among the junk — elastic bands, a rosary with a broken link, a nail file — a pendant on a cheap chain. Dull. Unremarkable.

24. CLOSE — 65mm, static
She picks it up because it's in the way of the torch batteries. Looks at it for a second the way you'd look at something you've owned for forty years and never worn.
She puts it on anyway. No reverence. It's a practical decision — she's packing, and it's smaller round her neck than in a bag.

25. STATIC WIDE — 35mm, locked off — INT. CORRIDOR — DAY
She walks the corridor, hand goes to her chest. First vision — recorded, not divine. Wrong aspect ratio, dropped frames, blown exposure and hiss. The thing she's ignored her whole life does something for the first time. Handheld only for the vision.

26. STATIC WIDE — 35mm, locked off — EXT. ST JUDE'S — DAY
She drives. Pendant bearing. The minibus on the empty road. Vision is tracker's recorded view, not divine. She pulls over, holds the pendant like it owes her money. The vision beat lands exactly where it was.

cast.name: Sister Nina Doyle
cast.description: Runs St Jude's, a residential house for people the system gave up on. Self-sufficient, can re-plumb a building, lies fluently to authority; gentle with the genuinely broken, brutal with anyone coasting. Daughter of the absconding rockstar, whom she never knew. The pendant is her mother's, always had it — not found on Deborah's bedside — and is the terminal's tracker. Half-angel and ineligible for sorting: nepotism, not tragedy. Faith is functional; God is her employer and she has views about management. Treats divine instruction as an unreliable supplier. Finds being called a saint ridiculous.

relations.note: Nina never knew her father; the pendant was the terminal's tracker.

cast.name: PC Kath Bridges
cast.description: White British police officer in her thirties. Sincerely believes she was left behind to teach moral justice; cannot remember who said so. Maintains paperwork and cites vanished superiors. Notices the wrong details with total commitment. Mild grievance, never fear or amazement. Thinks Ray is the one who gets carried away.

relations.note: Each thinks the other gets carried away.

cast.name: PC Ray Okonjo
cast.description: Black British police officer in his thirties. Sincerely believes he was left behind to teach moral justice; cannot remember who said so. Maintains paperwork and cites vanished superiors. Follows the wrong details nowhere. Mild grievance, never fear or amazement. Thinks Kath is the one who gets carried away.

relations.note: Each thinks the other gets carried away.

cast.name: Martin
cast.description: Failed musician in a denim jacket correct in 1994, hair long at the back on principle. Four guitars, nothing written in eleven years. Collected the rockstar's belongings at estate sales; won the terminal at auction and has it filed as period junk. Cannot reach his son. Aggrieved rather than grieving. Never learns what the machine is.

relations.note: Martin cannot reach his son; Max borrowed the terminal for a poster.

cast.name: Danny Crane
cast.description: Forty, olive waxed jacket, canvas satchel, untidy dark hair and stubble. Scavenging for water with his daughter Jodie. Has rules: nothing off anyone still alive. Cannot let her be right because the rules are the last bit of parenting he has. Keeps a laminated rules card. Dry and occupied by logistics, never played for grief.

relations.note: Father and daughter scavenging for water; rules versus practical experience.

cast.name: Jodie Crane
cast.description: Eleven, short sandy hair, navy hoodie under an oversized olive jacket, backpack and a headlamp on her collar. The headlamp stays off in Number Fourteen. Better at crime than Danny and knows it without cruelty. Sees his rules will get them killed. Her mother was raptured and judged worthy. No pathos performance.

relations.note: Father and daughter scavenging for water; rules versus practical experience.

cast.name: The absconder
cast.description: An angel who steals a terminal to live inside creation in 1980. Edits appearance, charisma, confidence and musical ability to the ceiling, leaves social status at default. Conjures a guitar; writes by entering tempo and key. Pockets the tracker off the machine's casing; in the montage, a flash of him fastening it round a girl's neck as a keepsake. Nina's father. Dies five years later and declines undo with NO. Prologue fix: shot 12 pockets tracker plus flash montage, shot 31 cut straight from ERROR to UNDO?. Appearance and age are not locked.

relations.note: Nina never knew her father; the pendant was the terminal's tracker.
